# Part 1 — Where it is now

## What it is

**GBIF Gap Finder** is a plug-and-play R pipeline and Shiny dashboard that lets any
(European) GBIF node generate a systematic gap analysis of their national biodiversity
data — identifying **where**, **when**, and **which species** are under-represented —
and explore the results interactively.

A node points the pipeline at its country's GBIF data, a national taxonomy backbone, and
(optionally) a red list and invasive-species registry, and gets a complete analysis with
minimal configuration.

## What works today (Sweden)

The full pipeline runs end-to-end for Sweden, and the dashboard is live with nine tabs.

**Pipeline** (scripts 00–14, with 01a/01b, 06a/06b and 09a/09a1/09b/09c splits):

| Stage | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Preflight (00) | ✅ | Checks every external dependency before a build; gates `tar_make()` |
| Ingestion (01–04) | ✅ | SQL-API cubes (17-col b-cubed superset) → parquet, shared EEA grids, GADM admin, provenance records |
| Validation (05) | ✅ | Parquet + column checks |
| Core summaries (06a/06b) | ✅ | Taxonomy-agnostic aggregations |
| Spatial gaps (07) | ✅ | Coverage, hotspots, zero-data cells |
| Temporal gaps (08) | ✅ | Recency, seasonality, trends |
| Reconciliation (09a/09a1) | ✅ | 5-tier matching (Tier 5 = Dyntaxa↔CoL crosswalk) → **99.8%** occurrence coverage |
| Taxonomic gaps (09b) | ✅ | Missing taxa, threat / establishment-means coverage |
| Scope summaries (09c) | ✅ | Four scopes (all / threatened / invasive / sensitive) + recent-period layer |
| Integration (10) | ✅ | Combined overview tables |
| App loader (11) | ✅ | Bundles the pre-computed files for the app (pure loader) |
| Reconciliation guardrail (12) | ✅ | Asserts headline numbers agree across layers; runs in `tar_make()` |
| Metrics snapshot (13) | ✅ | Refreshes `docs/metrics.md` from the output tables |
| Time points (04b, 14) | 🚧 | Historical snapshot cubes + gap closure for the Gaps filled tab (`run_timepoint.R`) |
| `targets` DAG | ✅ | Full `tar_make()` |
| Config system | ✅ | Country-aware `configs/config_{CC}.yml`, shared grids |

**Live dashboard tabs:** Overview · Priorities · Spatial · Temporal · Taxonomic ·
**Species of Concern** (Threatened / Invasive / Sensitive sub-tabs) · Publishers ·
Record Types · Data & Sources. A tenth tab, **Gaps filled**, is built and stays hidden
until the deployment sets `GAP_FINDER_SHOW_GAPS_FILLED=true`.

Also live: a **persona "start here"** entry that jumps users to the tabs relevant to their
role; **DOI + citation** for every dataset on the Data & Sources tab; selectable
**"All" / reset** on every taxonomy and kingdom filter; the three-category publisher
scheme (Citizen science · Private sector · Research data); and the Troudet sampling-bias
chart with a dominant-group exclusion filter.

**Four-layer taxonomy:** national backbone (Dyntaxa) + Red List threat status + Invasive
Species Registry + Sensitive Species List, unified via `in_dyntaxa`, `is_invasive`, and
`is_sensitive` flags.

## Current state

- **Version:** v0.8.0. Headline numbers reconcile across Overview / Taxonomic / Concern;
  `scripts/12_reconcile.R` checks this on every `tar_make()` (the `reconciliation` target)
  and on demand via `run_reconcile()`.
- **Gaps filled:** built and under review; hidden in the app until
  `GAP_FINDER_SHOW_GAPS_FILLED=true`.
- **Norway:** scaffolded (`config_NO.yml`, feature flags); not yet re-run against the
  current pipeline.
- **Disclaimer:** Built with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude).

## Design choices

- **Audience:** the broadest one — policy makers, researchers, funders, agencies and
  publishers, not only GBIF staff. Plain-language framing and EAA accessibility are part of
  the tool, not extras.
- **Partial year:** temporal charts default to the last *complete* year; the partial current
  year stays selectable, so a series does not end in a misleading drop.
- **Lowest taxonomic level:** family, as a filter (class → order → family) on the existing
  tables; there is no family × cell layer. Most tabs take family from the Catalogue of Life
  (the cube); Gaps filled takes it from Dyntaxa, its key space.
- **Invasive species** are shown at species level; order and family summaries say little
  for them.
- **Filters:** every filter has an explicit "All" / reset.
- **Citable data:** the GBIF download DOI is shown in the app, so users can cite and
  retrieve the exact data used.
- **Publishers:** the "GBIF Sweden" placeholder (a holding record for orphaned datasets) is
  left out of the publisher lists and charts; its records still count in the per-cell
  publisher dependency. Three categories: Citizen science · Private sector · Research data
  (universities, museums, herbaria, sequencing, field stations, marine institutes).
- **Grid:** the EEA reference grid (10 km / 50 km). Non-EEA grids are a possibility for
  other nodes (Part 2, C).
- **Navigation:** a "start here" entry routes each user group to the tabs that matter to it.

# Part 2 — What's still to come

Ordered from next up down to exploratory ideas.

## A. Next up

- [ ] 🚧 **Gaps filled — review and release.** Built (time points 2021-01-01, 2024-01-01
  and the live cube; closure tables from script 14) and hidden in the app meanwhile. Next:
  a current snapshot produced with the same query as the 2021 and 2024 snapshots, so
  long-term comparisons stay within one data source; then the review, and the tab switched
  on.

## B. Larger features (planned — scope & timing TBD)

> ⏸ Nothing in this section is scheduled.

### Snapshot-based pipeline
GBIF publishes complete monthly snapshots in Parquet.
- [ ] ⏸ **Generate cubes from snapshots** (DuckDB/Arrow) instead of SQL-API downloads — a
  self-contained pipeline with no manual download step. `04b` already builds the
  historical time-point cubes this way.
- [ ] ⏸ **Reproducibility without Zenodo** — archive code + config + snapshot date, not
  30 GB of derived data.

### Operations automation
- [ ] ⏸ Scheduled re-runs (cadence likely **half-yearly**), notification + auto-retry,
  auto-generated reports, deployment on the NRM server.

### Policy outputs layer
- [ ] ⏸ Annual Sweden **GBF Target 21** brief; EuropaBON / EBV national contribution
  report; multi-country Target 21 comparison (GBIF Secretariat handoff). Builds on the
  snapshot time series.

### Norway replication & country abstraction
- [ ] ⏸ Fill `config_NO.yml` DOIs; run end-to-end; document Sweden-specific assumptions
  that break.
- [ ] ⏸ Taxonomy / red-list **field abstraction** (generic DwC-A mapping, varying
  threat-status columns).
- [ ] ⏸ Generic **"bring your own grid"** support (cell-ID field + CRS config; remove
  EEA-specific assumptions).

## C. Additional ideas (exploratory / future possibility)

- [ ] ⏸ **CARE / Indigenous-data-governance tab** — flag cells overlapping Indigenous
  territories (e.g. Sámi), compare data density / recency / publisher diversity, surface in
  a "data equity" tab. **Must support data sovereignty, not surveil or extract** — needs
  GIDA-Sápmi consultation and ethical review. The app must not treat Sámi/Indigenous data
  as just another gap to mobilise.
- [ ] **EcoBon ecosystem cubes** — overlay ecosystem-level cubes to find under-sampled
  ecosystems; start with a data-availability + grid-alignment assessment.
- [ ] **EuropaBON / EBOCC alignment** — position node-level gap analysis as EuropaBON
  input; map to EBV workflow templates.
- [ ] **Non-EEA / global grids (for other nodes).** ISEA3H hexagonal grids via `dggridR`,
  taxonomy without a national backbone, sparse-data handling, and auto-generating a grid
  from the country boundary where none exists. A possibility for contributors; not on
  GBIF Sweden's own plan.
- [ ] **Uncertainty measures in the app** — surface the cube's coordinate / temporal
  uncertainty and distinct-observer measures in an app view.
- [ ] **Other analysis extensions** — 1 km resolution (major data-volume implications);
  PhyloPic silhouettes on charts; species-distribution-model coverage gaps; temporal trend
  predictions / forecasting; climate-envelope coverage (SMHI / Copernicus);
  cross-country comparison mode.
- [ ] **Other app features** — in-app PDF report generation; an API endpoint for
  programmatic gap-metric access.

## D. Standalone mini-projects (separate from the app)

- [ ] **Artportalen pre-1900 records** — quantify hobbyist-digitised specimen records
  (dated to 1551), link source specimens, flag duplicate / rights issues, so Artportalen
  can be informed and exports de-duplicated.

## Open questions

1. **Unicellular organisms** — excluded from the taxonomic gap (no backbone coverage);
   monitor future checklists.
2. **CARE metrics** — what does "CARE-aligned data" mean quantitatively? Needs GIDA-Sápmi
   consultation.
3. **EcoBon cubes** — data format, resolution, availability; EEA-grid compatibility?
